clue.text: On motorway, certain about coming accident

parts.note: the M1 motorway, read as MI, is the crossword standby for motorway

indicators.note: about tells us the word for certain goes round the word for coming

parts.note: certain means sure
advent is an arrival or coming

explanation.surface: A driver on the motorway is sure a crash is imminent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link but simply puts the motorway first; M1 is Britain's first motorway, its figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A misadventure is a mishap or unlucky event, much like an accident.

clue.text: Spirits of a sort holding up party procedures

indicators.note: holding means the spirits word contains the other piece

parts.note: meths is short for methylated spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for party is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a party is run on cheap alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Meths is British slang for methylated spirits, a cheap denatured alcohol. The printed clue lost its letter count (7).
explanation.definitionFit: Methods are systematic ways of doing things, which is what procedures are.

clue.text: Painting becomes firm after a short time

indicators.note: after places the firm's abbreviation behind the short time

parts.note: sec, short for second, is a short time
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Paint sets hard after a brief wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' is a link. Secco is painting done on dry plaster, as against fresco on wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Secco is a technique of wall decoration on dry plaster, so a kind of painting.

clue.text: Give two pounds, nothing more, to sculptor

parts.note: to donate is to give
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two of them are LL
O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An appeal asks for a modest gift of two pounds for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more' and 'to' are links. Donatello was a Florentine Renaissance sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a famous early Renaissance sculptor from Florence.

clue.text: Terrible ache in a head

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word ache is mangled into a new order

parts.note: the word ache is the fodder; that the solution also runs across 'Terrible ache' is a coincidence, the anagram being the intended reading

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a dreadful headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' looks like part of a headache; it means per person, as in 'five pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean per individual person, as in prices quoted per head.

clue.text: Scorers mentally switching parts

indicators.note: switching parts means the two portions of the word mentally swap places

explanation.surface: Scorekeepers do their sums in their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: MENTALLY splits into MEN and TALLY; 'switching parts' moves MEN to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallymen keep a tally, a running count, so they are scorers.

clue.text: Sounds like coarse fish

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the word is heard, not seen, giving a different spelling

parts.note: rough means coarse

explanation.surface: An angler sounds off about a coarse fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coarse fish' is an angling term, but 'coarse' is the word heard and 'fish' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruffe is a small European freshwater perch.

clue.text: Player given an awful roasting

indicators.note: awful signals that the word roasting is badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A performer gets a terrible slating from the critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roasting' looks like harsh criticism but is the fodder; 'given an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist plays the organ, so is a musical player.

clue.text: Inexperienced soldier that is attached to castle

parts.note: rook is another name for the chess piece called a castle
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A raw recruit is posted to a castle garrison.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a new recruit, a raw and untrained soldier.

clue.text: Teach 150 in special sort of college

indicators.note: special here means altered into a particular form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone teaches a hundred and fifty students at a specialist college.
explanation.walkthrough: TEACH, CL and IN together are rearranged by 'special'.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical college teaches practical and vocational subjects.

clue.text: Give up in pro game

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
go is a board game from East Asia

explanation.surface: A professional quits in the middle of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to do without or renounce something.

clue.text: City's side at sea in scoreless draw

indicators.note: in puts the ship's side inside the two zeros

parts.note: a nil-nil result is written 0-0, two Os
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A football team's players are all at sea in a goalless match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City's' is the definition with 's meaning 'has'. Oporto (Porto) is a Portuguese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, a city in northern Portugal.

clue.text: Sounds like obscure Scots explorer in London area

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for obscure is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to obscure something is to hide it
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: An unknown Scottish explorer turns up in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective (little-known) but is a verb. Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London.

clue.text: Cut lumber

definitions.meaning: a cut of meat such as lamb's back joint
to lumber someone is to burden them with something unwanted

explanation.surface: A woodworker saws timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is a joint of meat from the back; to saddle someone is to burden them.

clue.text: Release, in a manner of speaking

definitions.meaning: the act of handing over or letting go
the way a speaker utters words

explanation.surface: A statement issued, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery is both the handing over of goods and an orator's style of speech.

clue.text: Her pronouncement's relevant

indicators.note: pronouncement signals that the word for relevant is spoken, giving a name

parts.note: germane means relevant

explanation.surface: A woman's declaration is to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' is the definition: a woman's name, such as the writer Germaine Greer.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine is a woman's first name, so a 'her' in crossword terms.

clue.text: Cheese that's demonstrated success in long run

definitions.meaning: cheap, rubbery cheese, jokingly fit only to bait traps

definitions.text: that's demonstrated success in long run
definitions.meaning: Agatha Christie's play, which has run in London since 1952

explanation.surface: A cheese proves its worth over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap is slang for cheap cheese, and The Mousetrap is the world's longest-running play.

clue.text: A couple of boys in Essex town

parts.note: Basil is a boy's name
Don is another boy's name

explanation.surface: Two lads are found in a county town.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London; Basildon is one of its new towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Basildon is a new town in the English county of Essex.

clue.text: Something soothing spoken in castle

parts.note: a balm is a soothing ointment
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Soothing words are said inside a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is the British royal family's castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Clothing articles dropped by Boadicea

indicators.note: dropped by means the warrior queen's name loses those letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, so two articles give two As

explanation.surface: The ancient queen sheds her garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Boadicea was the queen of the Iceni who fought the Romans; take both As (one inside, one at the end) out of her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the upper part of a woman's dress, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Do some stock-taking with odd result

indicators.note: odd suggests the word result comes out strangely arranged

explanation.surface: An auditor's inventory gives a strange total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock-taking' looks like counting inventory; it is taking livestock, cattle theft.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal cattle, a humorous form of taking stock.

clue.text: Understanding contents of ten, in triplicate

indicators.note: contents of means only the inside is kept, discarding the outer letters

parts.note: ten written three times in a row

explanation.surface: Someone grasps what is in a set of forms filled out thrice.
explanation.walkthrough: Write TEN three times, TENTENTEN, then drop the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is an agreement or friendly accord between nations.

clue.text: Perfectly fit model of-pacifism to follow

parts.note: a dove is the symbol of peace and pacifism
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A peace activist in fine shape follows on.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'of-pacifism' is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: To dovetail is to join or interlock neatly, like a woodworking joint.

clue.text: Rebel who became US president

definitions.meaning: Wat ... led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
John ... was the tenth US president

explanation.surface: An insurgent rises to lead the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler was an English rebel leader; John Tyler a US president.

clue.text: Main force in Troy, for example

definitions.meaning: troy is a system of ... for precious metals

explanation.surface: The bulk of an army is camped at Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy' suggests the ancient city; it is troy weight, used for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight is heavy force, and troy is a standard measure of mass for gold and silver.

clue.text: For audience, could be chaps making appearance

indicators.note: for audience means what the listeners hear, a word sounding the same

parts.note: guys are chaps, men

explanation.surface: Some men turn up before a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward form or semblance.

clue.text: Endlessly on the go in Italian town

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: astir means up and about, busy

explanation.surface: Someone is constantly busy in an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a town in Piedmont, famous for its sparkling wine.

clue.text: Girl waits for its performance

definitions.meaning: waits are ... singers who go round at Christmas

explanation.surface: A girl waits to go on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waits' is a noun: Christmas street singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol is a woman's name, and a carol is the song Christmas singers perform.

clue.text: Waste one on flight

parts.note: a desert is a waste land
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bare piece of land lies on the flight path.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is running away from duty, a form of fleeing.

clue.text: First illustration shows face of building

definitions.meaning: a picture facing a book's title page
the decorated front or pediment of a building

explanation.surface: A book's opening picture shows the front of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontispiece is a book's opening plate and also an architectural facade.
